identity.what_this_segment_is: A 12-inch, 20 km connector/duplication line built by the Petroleum Pipelines Company (PPC) linking the north-south 'El-Tibeen/Assiut' oil-products trunk (GEM's P7325/P7334 family) to a fuel depot in El Minya governorate. It is one of three related Upper-Egypt products-pipeline projects the Ministry of Petroleum announced together in Dec 2021: (1) a 140 km Minya-Assiut doubling line, 750M EGP (= GEM P7316); (2) a 75 km Tebbin/Assiut renewal segment, 420M EGP (= GEM P7325); and (3) this 20 km doubling of the Tebbin/Assiut-to-Minya-depot connector, 88M EGP (= P7326, matches GEM's own Cost/Cost[ref] exactly). The Dec-2021 announcement names the destination depot as 'مستودع التعاون للبترول بالمنيا' (the 'Al-Ta'awun'/Cooperation Petroleum [Company] depot at Minya). A second, independently dated source (dostor.org, 29 Aug 2023, reporting on a PPC board meeting) separately confirms PPC was still discussing 'design, construction and operation of a 12-inch, 20 km El-Tibeen/Assiut products line in El Minya governorate' -- an exact spec match (diameter, length, trunk name, governorate) to this row, ~20 months after the original announcement, with no completion mentioned. A third GEM-cited source (petro-mag.org, Dec 2024 issue, article 'Petroleum Pipelines: Expansion in Infrastructure Projects' at p.138) shows PPC infrastructure expansion was still trade-press-current as of late 2024, but only the magazine's table-of-contents page could be read this session -- the article text itself was not retrieved.
identity.operator: Petroleum Pipelines Company (PPC / شركة أنابيب البترول), an EGPC subsidiary -- consistent with GEM's existing Owner field (Egyptian General Petroleum Corp [100%], EGPC being PPC's parent). PPC is the pipeline builder/operator; it is NOT ASORC (Assiut Petroleum Refining Company) -- ASORC's refinery is the trunk's downstream customer/destination, not the entity building or operating this connector. The receiving depot in Minya belongs to a separate, third company: 'التعاون للبترول' / 'الجمعية التعاونية للبترول' (the Petroleum Cooperative Society, founded 1934, a national fuel-marketing cooperative with an office/depot in every governorate) -- this is the offtake customer, not the pipeline operator.
identity.status_finding: GEM's 'construction' status looks still reasonably current but the project appears slow-moving: announced as under implementation in Dec 2021 (source 1), and as of the Aug 2023 PPC board article (source 2) the company was still described as 'discussing' ('تمت مناقشة') the design/construction/operation of this exact line, ~20 months later, with no completion mentioned in either source. No source located this session reports the line as operating/commissioned. Given only these two data points, 'construction' (i.e., not yet complete) is the best-supported reading; there's no evidence for a startup, but also no independent confirmation the project wasn't quietly finished sometime in 2024-2026 (the Dec-2024 petro-mag.org issue could not be read for detail this session).

start.name: Candidate tie-in point on the El-Tibeen/Assiut oil-products trunk nearest El Minya -- UNPINNED / not independently sourced
start.coord_source: Not independently geocoded and NOT confirmed. Derived only from GEM's own existing route geometry for the two adjacent trunk segments that carry the 'El-Tibeen/Assiut' name (P7325 'Beni Suef-Asyut Replacement segment', RouteAccuracy=low; P7334 'El-Tibeen-Asyut Oil Products Pipeline', RouteAccuracy=medium): both lines' nearest vertex to the El Minya depot (see 'end') sits at approximately this point, ~9.5 km away in a straight line, in the desert-edge corridor east of the Nile between El Minya and Mallawi. This is GEM's own geometry (never citable per standing rule 1) and is not tied to any independently named place, so it must be read as an inferred corridor direction only, not a confirmed endpoint. No Arabic or English source found this session names a specific town, station, or valve/pump site on the trunk near El Minya where this spur ties in.

end.name: El Minya depot (tank-farm / industrial site ~2 km SSW of El Minya city, on the Cairo-Aswan railway) -- most likely the 'مستودع التعاون للبترول' (Cooperation/Al-Ta'awun Petroleum Company depot) that the Dec-2021 announcement names as this line's destination
end.coord_source: OpenStreetMap, geocoded via Overpass API query for man_made=storage_tank and landuse=industrial within the El Minya bounding box: an 11-tank farm (ways 1004913273 through 1004913283, tagged building=yes + man_made=storage_tank) sits inside an unnamed landuse=industrial polygon (way 100024721), centroid approx. 28.0747N 30.7594E, ~2 km SSW of El Minya city center (OSM node 768032316, 28.0893N 30.7571E) and immediately adjacent to the Cairo-Aswan main railway (way 41986718). OSM carries no name/operator tag on this site, so its identity as specifically the Cooperation-Petroleum depot is inferred, not confirmed by OSM itself. Internal cross-check only (NOT a citable ref, per standing rule 1): this point sits within ~150 m of the point where GEM's own routes for the two adjacent OPERATING oil-products pipelines already meet -- P7320 'Beni Suef-El Minya Oil Products Pipeline' ends at (30.7594, 28.0750) and P7342 'El Minya-Asyut Oil Products Pipeline' begins at (30.7582, 28.0747) -- i.e. this tank farm is very likely the established general 'El Minya hub' depot on Egypt's Nile-valley products network. That convergence is a plausibility signal, not proof it is the exact facility this 20 km connector reaches.

corridor_note: If the trunk-side point above is accepted as a rough corridor direction, a candidate route would run roughly westward from the desert-edge trunk (~30.847, 28.110) into the tank-farm depot (~30.7595, 28.0748), a straight-line separation of ~9.5 km against the sheet's 20.00 km LengthKnownKm -- a ~2.1x corridor-to-straight-line ratio, which is plausible for an Egyptian Nile-valley connector following canals/roads/rail rather than a straight line (comparable ratios appear elsewhere in this tracker's Egypt routes, e.g. P7589 Faramid's 36.9 km corridor vs ~35 km straight separation). However, because the trunk-side point is inferred from GEM's own geometry rather than independently sourced, this is offered as a directional sanity check only -- NOT as a basis for drawing or staging an actual route geometry.
length_check: 20.00 km sheet length vs. ~9.5 km straight-line separation between the pinned depot end and the inferred trunk tie-in candidate: consistent (ratio ~2.1x), but only as a plausibility check, since one endpoint is unconfirmed.
notes: Two of the row's three data gaps are closed with reasonable confidence: identity (this is PPC's Tebbin/Assiut-to-Minya-depot duplication project, part of a documented 2021 Upper-Egypt pipeline package) and operator (PPC/EGPC, not ASORC). The geographic gap is only half-closed: the Minya depot end is pinned via independent OSM geocoding (medium confidence, corroborated internally -- not citably -- by GEM's own adjacent pipeline endpoints converging on the same spot), but the trunk-side tie-in has no independent source and should NOT be treated as resolved. Recommend against changing RouteAccuracy/RouteType or drawing a candidate geojson from this alone; the existing geometry:null placeholder and RouteAccuracy='no route' remain the honest state until either (a) an independent source names the trunk-side tie-in location, or (b) a routes-repo/human reviewer accepts the GEM-internal corridor as sufficient for a 'very low' schematic line. A follow-up worth trying: search for 'شركة التعاون للبترول فرع المنيا' or contact-page/address listings for the Cooperative Petroleum Society's Minya branch, which might name a specific site distinct from the inferred tank farm; also revisit petro-mag.org's Dec-2024 issue at article page 138, which this session could not open past its table of contents.
